Subject: Acme HS: initial proposal — early-unwind credit escrow + ramp schedule

Liam —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a proposed escrow construct and a redline of the term sheet that outlines an early-unwind credit bucket and a staggered ramp (60/30/10 over 3 months) that would allow Acme to downsize with predictable credits rather than an immediate termination charge. Highlights: 

- Escrowed credit bucket equal to 15% of the committed ARR, to be drawn down on a staged basis tied to ramp milestones.
- Staged ramp schedule: Month 1 at 60% of committed throughput; Month 2 at 30%; Month 3 at 10% — after which remaining commitment terminates.
- Opt-out language for pilot customers: 30-day notice with a pro-rated credit draw, subject to maximum escrow draw of 50% of the escrowed bucket.

I attached the escrow proposal (PDF) and a redline of the term sheet. Can you confirm whether Procurement/legal at Acme needs the escrow provider to be on their approved vendor list? Also, if there are any internal approval hurdles on the credit ceiling we should know about.

If you want, Dylan can join a quick call this afternoon to walk through the mechanics. Next step from our side: internal approval from leadership for the credit cap and the opt-out carveout.

Thanks,

Team —

Putting this thread into the deal-desk queue. Acme is asking for an escrow-backed early-unwind credit bucket (initial ask 15% ARR) with a staged ramp schedule. Quick summary and recommended ask for leadership approval: 

- Customer: Acme Health Systems, Deal ID ACM-2028-1197 (Large strategic healthcare account).
- Proposal: 15% escrowed credit bucket, drawn down as customer steps through 60/30/10 ramp months. Opt-out requires 30-day notice; escrow draw cap at 50% of bucket (they cannot draw more than half).
- Risk/Exposure: If fully drawn to cap, Redwood's max one-time credit expense = 7.5% of committed ARR (i.e., 50% of 15%).
- Business reasons to grant: preserves relationship and runway for them to shift traffic; increases likelihood of renewal/expansion later; preserves public-case study potential.
- Conditions we should insist on: escrow held by independent provider approved by Acme; written SOW showing traffic ramp milestones; finance review and runbook for credit application; limit to one use per 12-month term.

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_redline.docx (contains our redlines and suggested protective language).

Ask for Jonas/leadership: approval to offer the 15% escrow with the following required constraints: (1) escrow draw capped at 50% of bucket, (2) escrow held by approved third-party, (3) SOW milestone verification, (4) one-time use per term, and (5) legal to sign final redline. If leadership prefers lower exposure, suggest approving 10% bucket instead.

If approved, I'll coordinate with Legal and Finance to prepare the vendor onboarding packet and the short finance explainer Liam requested.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Director, Enterprise Sales

Team —

After reviewing the note and the exposure math, I approve offering an escrowed credit bucket with the following three binding conditions: 

1) Reduce the escrow bucket to 12% of committed ARR (compromise between 15% ask and Finance concerns).
2) Escrow draw cap remains at 50% of the bucket (so max immediate exposure = 6% of ARR).
3) Acceptance requires: third-party escrow provider (must pass Acme vendor onboarding), signed SOW with objective ramp milestones and verification checkpoints, one-time use per 12-month contract term, and Legal approval on the final redline.

We should also add a clause: if Acme resumes >75% of committed throughput within 6 months, any unused escrowed credits are returned to Redwood. That protects us for rapid reversions.

Dylan — please coordinate the updated term sheet (12% bucket) and loop Legal; Marissa, please share the finance explainer (sample dollar math) with Liam and Procurement. Once Legal signs off we can send the corrected redline to Acme and introduce the escrow provider to their procurement team.
